title: Show me proof, said the man who had decided already.
subtitle: Asking for evidence with the door already shut

row.title: Fir'awn
sub: bring a sign, if you are truthful

row.title: I want proof
sub: but I will not believe anyway

then: Musa stood before Fir'awn and his court and said he was a messenger from the Lord of all that exists. He asked for the Children of Israel to be freed. Ibn Kathir explains that Fir'awn had {trap}already refused to believe or grant the request{/trap}, and only demanded a sign to see if the claim held up.
now: Someone sends you a long, careful article that challenges a habit of yours. You type back: send me a source. They send three. You skim one and close the tab. {idea}The question was never about evidence.{/idea} It was about whether you were willing to move.
old: I just need more proof before I change anything.
new: Asking for proof only means something if I am ready to act on it.
try: Pick one thing you keep asking proof for. Ask yourself honestly: what would I do if I got it?

title: A plain staff became the sign no one could deny.
subtitle: The answer came in front of everyone
then: Fir'awn asked for a sign, and Musa threw down his staff. Ibn Kathir reports from Ibn 'Abbas that it became a huge serpent that rushed toward Fir'awn, who {trap}jumped from his throne and cried to Musa for help{/trap}. The man who claimed to be lord could not hold his seat.
now: You walk into a meeting with someone who controls your contract. Their office, their rules, their tone. It all feels permanent. Then one email from above changes everything in a minute. {idea}What looks unshakable is held up by Allah, and can be moved by Him.{/idea}
old: The people with power over me are the ones really in control.
new: Every throne sits on ground that belongs to Allah.
try: Next time you feel small before someone powerful, quietly say: Allah is greater. Then speak calmly.

title: His hand came out shining, and not from sickness.
subtitle: A second sign, gentle and bright
then: After the staff, Musa drew his hand from his cloak and it shone white for the onlookers. Ibn Kathir notes, citing 27:12, that it was {idea}bright without any hurt{/idea}, not leprosy or disease. He put it back, and it returned to its usual color.
now: Some lessons come to you loud: a scare at the doctor, a lost job. Others come quiet: a stranger's kindness on a bad day, a line in a book at the right moment. {reward}Both are signs.{/reward} The quiet ones are easier to walk past.
old: Only dramatic moments count as a message from Allah.
new: Allah shows His signs in fear and in light, and both deserve attention.
try: Tonight, write down one small, gentle good thing from today that you almost missed.

title: When the truth was clear, they gave it a label.
subtitle: Calling it magic so they could ignore it
then: Once Fir'awn felt safe and returned to his throne, he told his chiefs this was a well-versed sorcerer, and they agreed. Ibn Kathir says they {trap}plotted to portray Musa as a liar and a fake{/trap}, to put out the light he brought.
now: A friend points out, kindly, that you snap at your kids when you are tired. You say: oh, she is just being dramatic. One word, and the point is gone. {trap}A label is a quick way to not listen.{/trap}
old: If I can name what is wrong with the messenger, I can ignore the message.
new: Dismissing the speaker does not make the truth go away.
try: Recall one piece of advice you dismissed by labeling the person. Think about the advice itself for two minutes.

title: They turned a call to worship into a threat to land.
subtitle: Fear of losing position, dressed up as defense
then: The chiefs told the people that Musa wanted to drive them out of their land through magic. Ibn Kathir says they feared he would win people over and prevail over them. Citing 28:6, he notes that {trap}what they feared is exactly what came to them{/trap}.
now: A new colleague suggests a fairer way to share the workload. Instead of asking if it is fair, you hear: they are after my role. You start talking about them in the break room. {idea}Fear of losing a position can make good advice sound like an attack.{/idea}
old: Anyone who changes things here is a threat to me.
new: Before I fight a change, I should check if I am only guarding my own place.
try: Think of one change at work or home you resisted. Ask: was it bad, or just bad for my ego?

title: Delay him, they said, and gather the experts.
subtitle: Buying time instead of facing the truth

row.title: it is the same trick
sub: we can beat it with ours

then: The chiefs advised Fir'awn to delay Musa and his brother and send gatherers through the provinces. Ibn Kathir explains that {trap}magic was widespread and popular then{/trap}, and they wrongly assumed Musa's signs were the same kind of thing, so they could be beaten the same way.
now: A doctor tells you to change how you eat. You say, let me think about it, and start reading every article that says you are fine. {trap}Delay plus a search for the answer you want.{/trap} It feels like research. It is a way to avoid the decision.
old: I will wait and find someone who tells me otherwise.
new: Postponing the truth while I shop for opinions is still a refusal.
try: Name one thing you are putting off deciding. Set a date this week to decide it.

title: Every expert in the land, against one man and Allah.
subtitle: Gathering numbers to drown out the truth

row.title: one staff
sub: and the One who sent it

then: The plan was to bring every skilled sorcerer to Fir'awn. Ibn Kathir links this to 20:58-60, where Fir'awn set a meeting on a festival day in front of the people. {trap}He gathered his plot{/trap}, sure that numbers and skill would win.
now: You are the only one in the office who will not fudge the expense report. Everyone else has a reason, and there are more of them. It starts to feel like you are the strange one. {idea}How many agree has never been the measure of what is right.{/idea}
old: If everyone around me thinks it is fine, it must be fine.
new: A crowd of experts cannot make falsehood true.
try: Next time you are outnumbered on something you know is right, stay kind and stay put.

title: The first thing the magicians asked about was pay.
subtitle: Working for whoever pays, before the truth showed
then: The sorcerers came to Fir'awn, and before anything else they asked about their reward if they won. Ibn Kathir says Fir'awn {reward}promised them tremendous provisions{/reward} and made them hope for what they wished for. Their skill was for hire.
now: A client offers you a big bonus to write reviews for a product you have never used. The first question in your head is: how much? {trap}The question about right and wrong comes second, if at all.{/trap}
old: If the pay is good, the job is fine.
new: The first question about any work should be whether it is right, not what it pays.
try: Look at one task you do for money. Ask once, plainly: would I do this if it were seen by Allah? Then decide.

title: Yes, and you will be close to me, said Fir'awn.
subtitle: The lure of money and an inner circle
then: Fir'awn did not only promise money. Ibn Kathir explains he promised to make them {reward}among his private audience and best associates{/reward}. Status and closeness to power were the real hook.
now: Your boss hints you could join the leadership group if you back a decision you know is unfair. A seat at the table. Your name on the invite list. {trap}Belonging can be a stronger bribe than cash.{/trap}
old: Being close to the important people is worth a small compromise.
new: Closeness bought by betraying the truth is distance from Allah.
try: Notice one circle you want to be part of. Ask what it costs you to stay in it.

title: You throw first, or shall we? They came confident.
subtitle: The challenge on the festival day
then: On the appointed day, the magicians faced Musa and offered him the choice of who would throw first. Ibn Kathir notes that in 20:65 they offered to be the first. {trap}They were sure of their craft{/trap} and of the crowd watching.
now: You walk into an argument with your spouse fully loaded: dates, receipts, screenshots. You are certain you will win. {idea}Being prepared is not the same as being right.{/idea}
old: If I am skilled and prepared, I will win.
new: Skill used against the truth only delays the moment it loses.
try: Before your next disagreement, ask yourself first: what if I am the one who is wrong here?

title: They fooled the eyes, but the ropes were still ropes.
subtitle: A great show that was only an illusion
then: Musa told them to throw first. Ibn Kathir gives the wisdom: the people would see the sorcery first, so the truth would land harder when it came. Ibn 'Abbas said they threw ropes and sticks that {trap}appeared to crawl, an illusion{/trap} that struck terror into the crowd.
now: A feed full of perfect homes, perfect bodies, perfect marriages. Filters, angles, edits. You close the app feeling behind on everything. {trap}The ropes look like snakes.{/trap} {idea}Your eyes were played, but your life did not change.{/idea}
old: What I see on the screen is how things really are.
new: A great show can bewitch my eyes without being real.
try: Next time a post makes you feel less, say to yourself: rope, not snake. Then put the phone down.

title: One staff swallowed every lie they had thrown.
subtitle: Truth does not argue with illusion, it ends it
then: At that moment Allah inspired Musa to throw his staff. Ibn Ishaq said it {idea}followed the ropes and sticks one after another until nothing remained{/idea}, then became a staff again in his hand. The magicians knew this was not magic.
now: Your head is full of rope-snakes at 2am: they all think I am a failure, I will never fix this, it is too late. Then one true thought lands: Allah sees me and the door of repentance is open. {reward}One truth can swallow a dozen fears.{/reward}
old: There are too many problems for anything to fix them.
new: One truth from Allah outweighs any number of illusions.
try: Write down your loudest fear. Next to it, write one thing Allah says that answers it.

title: The truth stood, and all their work came to nothing.
subtitle: Effort spent against the truth is lost
then: The magicians had trained, traveled, and performed their best. In one moment, {idea}the truth was confirmed{/idea}, and {trap}all that they did was made of no effect{/trap}. Ibn Kathir calls it the moment Allah separated truth from falsehood.
now: Months spent building a cover story, keeping a version of yourself alive for people's approval. Then one honest conversation, and the whole structure falls. {trap}All that effort was for something that could not stand.{/trap}
old: If I put in enough effort, it will hold.
new: Only what is built on truth survives the moment truth appears.
try: Ask yourself which of your daily efforts would still matter if everything hidden were seen. Give that one more time.

title: Right there, in front of everyone, they were beaten.
subtitle: The festival meant to shame Musa shamed Fir'awn

row.title: Allah
sub: used it to show the truth

then: Fir'awn had chosen a festival day so the people could watch Musa fail. Instead, {trap}Fir'awn and his people were defeated there and returned humbled{/trap}. The crowd he gathered became witnesses against him.
now: You plan to show up a coworker in the big meeting, with slides ready to prove them wrong. The facts come out in their favor, in front of everyone you invited. {idea}Plans to humiliate others have a way of turning around.{/idea}
old: If I set it up right, I can make them look bad.
new: Whoever sets a stage against the truth ends up on it.
try: If you are planning to prove someone wrong in public, talk to them privately first.

title: The experts were the first to fall in prostration.
subtitle: Those who knew magic best recognized what was not
then: The magicians realized this was from heaven and by no means magic. Ibn Ishaq reports they said: had Musa been a magician, he would not have beaten us. {reward}They fell down prostrate{/reward}, the same people who had asked for a fee that morning.
now: You are the accountant who can tell when the numbers are real, the nurse who can tell when a patient is truly sick. {idea}Your expertise can lead you to the truth faster than anyone{/idea}, if you let it, instead of using it to hide.
old: What I know is just a skill I sell.
new: Real knowledge should bring me to my knees before Allah, not keep me standing proud.
try: In your field, notice one thing that shows Allah's design. Make a short sujud of thanks for it today.
